title: Funds: restricted and unrestricted money
summary: Track money by fund, release restricted money once it is spent on its purpose, and move money between funds.

steps.text: A fund is a pot of money you track on its own. A restricted fund holds gifts a donor limited to a purpose. An unrestricted fund holds money you set aside for a use of your own, and you can spend or move it as you decide. Money on no fund shows as {unres}.
To start, open {settings}, choose the {funds} tab and turn funds on. Until you do, nothing carries a fund. {off} works again only once every fund is back to zero.

Click {add} and name the fund. Tick {restricted} when a donor limited what the money may be spent on, and write the {purpose}. Once anything is posted to a fund, whether it is restricted and its purpose can't change. {archive} stops new postings to a fund that holds nothing; {unarchive} brings it back.

On an invoice, bill or journal entry, pick a fund in the {fund} column to put a line on that fund. A line left empty shows as {unres}. A record from outside, such as one from a connection, can also be put on one fund as a whole.
When you start using funds, use {opening} to give part of each account's balance to a fund as at the {date}. Each line takes the amount from money with no fund.

capture.selector: main details:has(> summary:has-text('Opening balances by fund'))

steps.text: Use {transfer} to move money between two unrestricted funds, or between a fund and money with no fund, for example to set money aside for a project or to give it back.

Use {release} once restricted money has been spent on its purpose. First post that purpose spending with no fund, as an ordinary bill or journal entry. Then tick it in the list of spending the release shows: the release moves that amount from the restricted fund to an unrestricted one and names the spending it pays for.
Use {realloc} only to move restricted money to another restricted fund with the same purpose, and only when the donor has agreed in writing. Enter that agreement under {auth}.
Each movement posts its own journal entry with the {reason} you give. To undo one, open {activity} from {reports}, find it under {movements} and click {reverse}.

Records that arrive from a connection, a file import or your accountant wait for a fund choice until you pick one. To skip the wait, set default funds on the connection under Settings, Connectors: its records then take that fund when they arrive.
If a record from outside already posted on the wrong fund, open it and change its fund, giving a reason. Its entries are voided and posted again on the new fund.

Three reports cover funds. {bs} shows each account by fund, with each fund's net assets and how much is restricted. {act} shows what each fund received, spent, released and transferred. {rec} checks that the funds add up to the company ledger.

You can also ask the assistant to create or archive a fund, move money between funds, release restricted money or read a fund report. It shows each change as a card and makes it only when you confirm.
